statement0:
The word "graph" is mentioned two or more times in 0.9% of psychology papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "graph" , 27.9% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a somewhat higher rate than the median Psychology paper (median shown for reference); relative to other words, papers with "graph" are in the top 69th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability. Among papers where under 32% of significant p-values are fragile, the rate of successful replication was found to be 59.5%, whereas for papers over the replication rate was just 33.8% (see Supplemental Materials 7.3 of the mentioned paper).
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "graph" tend to be published in higher impact factor journals (95th percentile among all words) but tend to be cited less (45th percentile word). In general, this word is negatively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are less likely to publish papers containing "graph" (44th percentile).
